chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married off his slave girl to a free man, or to a slave of other people. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not for him to remove her. So if he sells her, and the one who buys her wishes to remove her from her husband, he may do so.'
ai.seo_question: Can a master divorce his slave wife from her husband if he sells her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the marital stability of a female slave (umm walad or simply slave woman) once married with her master's permission, establishing that the master loses the right to unilaterally dissolve the union. It highlights the legal principle that the master's ownership is tied to the marital bond, but this bond is contingent on his continued ownership; thus, if he sells her, the new owner inherits the right to separate her from her husband, reflecting the flexible yet structured nature of slavery in Shia jurisprudence.
